Authorization (who may report which scope) is intentionally left to the DM-171 commands; this ticket enforces what any stored observation must be. Read order is (recordedAt, id), deterministic on every machine. Shared contract edited (space.ts/contract.ts): three optional fields only, existing records unchanged; the DM-169 fixture's corrective_effort_ms moved its cause from attributes to the typed field (DM-169 scripts still pass). evidence.notes:
Design notes for reviewers and later tickets:
- Span attributes the projection reads: spanStart (ISO), role (worker|orchestrator|reviewer|other; default worker when scoped to an attempt, else other), handle (stream identity), waitKind on wait_ms (queue|build_test|blocked|review|human_approval). Host adapters should send role and handle. Without a handle, parallel workers stay separate (keyed by attempt) and orchestrator spans are keyed by role, so one orchestrator is not counted once per attempt (the earlier run's actorKeyOf defect).
- Sprint totals use one membership rule for everything (the attempt's plan revision; non-attempt spans by their scope.sprintId, else the ticket's sprint). Sprint waits are summed over tickets (ticket-ms) plus the checkpoint wait. A ticket whose sprint id changed by adoption gets no readiness (lead time missing), rather than an invented window.
- Readiness is derived in the service only where records show it (sprint activation and acceptance of every dependency). Otherwise lead time and waitBeforeDispatch are missing.
- Failed/canceled end times come from the event log; the row's updated_at (later rewritten by supersession or reconciliation) is only a fallback for runs imported without their local log.
- Spans scoped to an attempt count as its effort from the claim to the end of its review or reconciliation, so reviewer work after submit is the attempt's overhead. Span time outside that window is reported as outsideWindowMs, not counted.
- Delta/cumulative active_ms has no place in time and is listed as not_an_interval (not counted here).
- I did not run the full suite, coverage, build or Fireguard (left to the testing tail).

outputs.summary: Adds a pure timing projection and its run feed, in commit e1f1165 on space-DM-172. projectTiming (src/core/space/timing.ts, helpers timingIntervals.ts and timingActivity.ts) takes server lifecycle events plus host/agent active_ms and wait_ms span events (spanStart, else observedAt minus the value, to observedAt) and returns classified segments and totals per attempt, ticket, sprint and run as of a cutoff. Claim-to-submit is attempt_elapsed only; active time is only where the attempt worker's activity spans cover it. Classes: active, queue (ready and unclaimed, awaiting reconciliation), build_test, blocked (run paused, host-reported), review (submitted, undecided), human_approval (sprint checkpoint, retry grant, host prompt), unknown (reason after_last_signal or no_activity_evidence). Inside an attempt: activity > host wait > pause > unknown. There is no waste class. Missing stops end at the run end, else the cutoff (open). An expired lease ends at its deadline, or at the takeover that expired it. Duplicates and out-of-order input are ordered, deduplicated (the first delivery of an observation id wins) and listed in anomalies. Nothing is negative or counted after the cutoff. Every number is a TimingQuantity (src/shared/domain/timing.ts) with a distinct kind type, unit, aggregation (single/union/sum), state (observed/estimated/partial/missing), coverage and open flag. A missing value is null and covers 0. Effort is summed over streams (source+actor+handle; without a handle, worker spans are keyed by attempt and other roles by role). It is reported beside the in-flight and active wall-clock unions and the sprint/run elapsed windows. Orchestrator, reviewer and other overhead is listed byRole and as overhead. Nested inclusive usage is not counted twice. Failed, rejected, canceled, expired and superseded attempts keep their elapsed time, effort and unknown time (effortByOutcome, with unreported counts). Carried-forward attempts are listed and not counted. Sprints assign everything by the attempt's plan revision (membership: attempt_revision). projectRunTiming(ctx, {runId, asOf?}) (src/core/services/timing.ts, capability read) feeds the projection from portable rows (attempts, runs, sprint_reports, approvals, checkpoints), the local event log (pauses, takeover, progress notes, retry grants, exact failure/cancel times) and the run's ledger observations. It has no caller yet: wiring it into IPC/MCP/grading belongs to later tickets. Checked-in clock fixtures: src/core/space/fixtures/timing/*.json (8 scenarios with expectations). Rules: docs/space-grading.md 'Time and effort'. No existing module was modified (only docs/space-grading.md), so no existing Vitest file covers the change; tests are left to the testing tail.

outputs.summary: Attempt 2 fixes every rejection reason, in commit 49b7672 on top of attempt 1 (e1f1165). The design is unchanged: pure projectTiming (src/core/space/timing.ts, helpers timingIntervals.ts and timingActivity.ts), types in src/shared/domain/timing.ts, run feed projectRunTiming (src/core/services/timing.ts, no caller yet). B1: a carried-forward ticket (a non-superseded carry_forward attempt and no attempt of its own in this run) accrues no time: no segments, lead time, cycle time or dispatch wait (TicketTiming.carriedForward). The service emits only the claim and any supersession for carry-forward rows, so there is no spurious accepted event or anomaly. B2: one sprint rule for every total (SprintTiming.membership 'current_plan'). A ticket, with all its attempts, segments and spans, belongs to the sprint that holds it in the run's current plan. A ticket the current plan no longer holds keeps its last attempt's sprint. The service loads every revision the run used (current, attempts' revisions, logged run.revision_adopted from/to) and maps older sprint ids to current ones the way adoption maps the active sprint: same id, else same ordinal (TimingInput.sprintAliases). Activations, reports, approvals, claims, span scopes and readiness all use the mapped ids. An id with no counterpart, or a ticket in no sprint, is listed as an 'unattributed' anomaly, never silently dropped. B3: an inclusive parent span gives up the time its descendants (usage parentActor chains) report, instead of the children losing theirs. B4: the projection is now linear. Spans are grouped by attempt and ticket once; descendant covers are memoised per actor; cuts are found by binary search; classification sorts layer edges once into numeric segments; tickets classify an outline with attempt placeholders and splice in the attempts' segments; ISO formatting is exact and about 5x faster. Measured cold in this environment: 20,000 attempts x 1 span 767 ms (was 70.7 s for the reviewer), 1 attempt x 20,000 spans 156 ms, nested 10k+10k 111 ms. N1: a lease expiry ends the attempt at its deadline even after a reconcile resubmit. The deadline comes from the attempt.lease_expired payload, else the row, else the takeover; the resubmission is then reviewed. N2: effort buckets (attempt outcome, 'superseded', 'unscoped' for spans scoped to no attempt) allocate each stream's union once, so they add up to effort.total. N3: nothing to measure (no span, no attempt, no window) reads missing, never 0 observed (0/0). N4: overhead coverage counts reviewed attempts that have an overhead span, and is estimated only from overhead streams. N5: an agent's report of an identity the host also reports is dropped (duplicate_source anomaly). N6: run-scoped overhead in no sprint is RunTiming.unattributedEffort, shown per sprint as unattributedOverhead, never in sprint effort. N7: projectRunTiming clamps asOf to now. N8: 'after_cutoff' removed. New fixtures: carried-forward, renamed-sprint, inclusive-parent-worker, host-and-agent, lease-resubmit; nested-usage and overlapping-workers are updated. reasons: c4 BLOCKING: a second `dm usage --run X --unavailable <host>` always fails with conflict (src/cli/usage.ts:119-144): observedAt is now, so the same delivery id gets a different payload each call; the orchestration bucket is sent first, so attempts claimed after the first call can never be marked (claim t1, mark, claim t2, mark -> conflict, attempt 2 unreported). Use a stable observedAt or skip buckets already marked; make the call safely repeatable.

c1 BLOCKING: the attribute budget ignores server-added attributes (hostUsage.ts:344-359,400 vs metricReports.ts:107-111): tokens_total is filled to 20 then the server adds `overhead` (+`sourceEvent` for deltas) -> 21 -> invalid_input; triggered by >=16 unknown usage fields (Anthropic, e.g. iterations[]) or >=14 (OMP) on main/unattributed threads, so orchestration is never recorded. Reserve the server's slots and degrade gracefully (drop lowest-priority raw.* fields) instead of failing.

c3 BLOCKING: one host session that orchestrates two runs double counts (hostAttribution.ts:136-147,234): the whole main thread becomes orchestration in every linked run and the other run's workers become unattributed in each (session spent 83,000; each run totals 83,000). Bound the main thread by the run's link window (from its first link event to the next run's), drop other-run claims, and demonstrate with run 1 canceled + run 2 in the same session (this host's real situation).

c2: a retry in the same thread binds only at the first answered attempt call (hostTranscripts.ts:108-118,213-227); the message handing over the new claim token is not read, so usage after a rejection stays on the rejected attempt (live: one request per retry, 234k-412k tokens; synthetic: 116,000/1,500 vs true 20,000/97,500). Bind at the earliest point the new token appears in the thread (the incoming message), and `start_run` should link too (hostTranscripts.ts:119-121) as the docs say.

c3/c4: (a) Claude spans close early when a non-waiting tool or permission wait exceeds 15 minutes, then the same event id conflicts forever (hostAttribution.ts:214,223; hostTranscripts.ts:350-362): track open tools like OMP, never emit a span that can later change; (b) `--unavailable` marks the orchestration bucket unconditionally and flips an observed 30000 total to missing irreversibly (usage.ts:141-144): mark only buckets with no real usage; (c) reads skip the last 15 minutes / last Claude message while cells read observed (usage.ts:25): mark the unsettled tail as unreported/partial rather than observed, and document a read after the settle time; (d) cumulativeDeltas treats unknown numeric fields as running totals (raw.tool_calls 15 vs 8; hostUsage.ts:239-248): only delta known cumulative token fields.

evidence.notes:
Design decisions for the reviewer: (a) A check has no per-check review channel, so a check reported on an accepted attempt is reviewer_checked, while a criterion is reviewer_checked only when the reviewer passed it to accept_attempt. Decisions recorded before this change have no decision.criteria, so their criteria read as worker claims (honest, but older accepted tickets read verification missing). (b) Independence rests on the attempt.review capability; decidedBy labels are not compared, because the orchestrator and workers can share a label. (c) ticketFailed comes from the current execution state and applies only when the chosen attempt is the final one. (d) Failed, canceled and lease-expired attempts are rewound by updated_at, which a later supersede or reconcile can move. (e) Required checks use the current Definition of Done, as the gate does. (f) A defect found in another epic is recorded in its origin epic, because evidence must belong to the observation epic. outputs.summary:
P inputs and escaped defects, one commit (1aeeec6) on space-DM-175.

(1) Verification read model, pure (src/core/space/verification.ts, ticketPerformance): every criterion of the plan revision the attempt ran under (cited as criterion ticket+c1) and every reported check (check attempt+name) gets a basis: reviewer_checked (a criterion the reviewer passed to accept_attempt; a check reported on an accepted attempt), worker_claim, skipped or missing. The state is verified/reviewed, failed/confirmed_failure (a reviewer-checked failure, or the ticket used every try, counted from the end of its final attempt), missing/worker_claims_only or required_evidence_missing (a sprint acceptance node needs its Definition of Done; sprintDefinition is now exported from checkpoints.ts), pending/awaiting_review, in_progress or awaiting_retry, missing/carried_forward or no_attempt. Each attempt is rewound to the cutoff. Independence comes from the attempt.review capability, which no worker holds. acceptAttempt now also keeps the reviewer criteria on the decision (decision.criteria, left out when none are passed; the portable schema already allowed it), so reviewer-checked criteria stay apart from worker claims.

(2) Escaped defects are escaped_defect ledger observations with a vocabulary that the ledger enforces on record and on import (defectProblem in src/core/space/defects.ts, called from ledgerProblem). defectEvent is report (value 1: severity, attribution attributed/candidate/unassigned, discoveryPhase, optional defectKey, exactly one commit with detail source build, and an origin that fits the attribution) or duplicate/reassessment/fix/withdrawal (value 0, each citing its report with detail defect). observations.ts refuses an attributed origin attempt that is not an accepted work attempt of the origin ticket. resolveDefects reads only records stored by the cutoff. A defect keeps its first report id. A shared defectKey or a duplicate record folds reports into it, so a defect counts once. Records link by reference, so a report and its withdrawal sent in one call read correctly with random or descending ids, and nothing is derived from stored rows at record time, so a retry is a no-op. Reassessments apply in (recordedAt, observedAt, id) order. A fix keeps the defect counted (status fixed); a withdrawal uncounts it. Nothing is deleted.

(3) Charging: only an attributed defect naming the standing accepted attempt and found after its decision is charged. Candidates, unassigned defects, defects of other outcomes and defects found before acceptance are passed to gradeSpace as unassigned (shown, not charged). The input carries cutoff and basisAt, so a later confirmed regression is a new dated input, and earlier cutoffs rebuild identically.

(4) Services in src/core/services/performance.ts, read-only, capability read: getTicketPerformance and getEscapedDefects (cutoff clamped to now, invalid cutoff gives invalid_input). There is no command or MCP tool yet: DM-179 and DM-266 own exposure. Types are in src/shared/domain/performance.ts. Docs: space-grading.md has a new section Verification and escaped defects (P inputs); architecture.md covers decision.criteria and the defect vocabulary.

outputs.summary:
Fix round, commit ae799d9 on top of 1aeeec6 (attempt 1; its summary still applies except where noted). Every rejection reason is fixed:
(1) Who may change charging. Defect records that change charging (an attributed report, a duplicate, a reassessment, a fix, a withdrawal) now need a human or server source, or a server-stamped attribute authority: review. recordAttemptMetrics/recordRunMetrics add the stamp only when the session holds attempt.review (orchestrator, reviewer); a worker gets unauthorized, and a caller-set stamp is invalid_input. defectProblem (the ledger, so import too) refuses unstamped agent/host records, and resolveDefects ignores any that exist. Repro adv2 is now refused: ticket 2 stays charged. A reviewer withdrawal is stamped and takes effect.
(2) Same cutoff, same input. The verification rewind no longer reads updated_at, current execution state or current config. It uses: failure times from attempt.failed events; cancel times from run.canceled/run.failed canceledAttempts, else the run ended_at; lease expiry from the deadline or the takeover; reconciled_at/superseded_at/decided_at/submitted_at columns; retry grants by their ticket.retry_granted time (grants with no local log entry count as earlier); the retry limit of the attempt revision. The Definition of Done an acceptance node was accepted against is frozen on its decision (decision.requiredChecks, optional in the portable schema). acceptAttempt also always writes decision.criteria ([] when none). sprintDefinition moved to increments.ts. The four adv.ts repros (A grantRetry, B abandon, C supersede, D DoD change) now read identical. Documented limits: a failure recorded on another machine has no local log entry and is timed by the row update; records imported later carry their own recordedAt.
(3) Only frozen Definition of Done checks and reviewer-unmet criteria confirm a failure. Any other failed check is a required:false diagnostic: a pre-existing failure on an accepted attempt reads verified.
(4) Legacy accepts (no decision.criteria) read missing/legacy_review_basis_unknown, criteria basis review_unknown.
(5) Also fixed. N3: every escaped_defect record must name an epic. N4: a conflicting report under one defectKey stays its own defect, with a conflicting_reports anomaly. N5: a withdrawal withdraws only the report it cites (EscapedDefect.withdrawals); the defect reads its earliest live report and counts while one remains. N6: before_acceptance compares server recordedAt. N7: an ended run with no outcome reads missing/run_ended. N8: self_duplicate is removed. Same-call reassessments now apply in ledger order (recordedAt, id), which is call order for server ids.
Fixtures were updated to the new facts shape (attempt reconciledAt/endedAt/retryLimit, retryGrants, runEnded; DoD on the decision; non-DoD checks required:false). Docs (space-grading.md, architecture.md), the record_attempt_metrics description and the space.ts comments were updated.

decision.notes: All five criteria met as demonstrated; rejected for D1-D3 (real projects with backlog epics or empty runs lose totals) and read cost the dashboard needs. Decisions accepted: exact-match comparability; unplanned epic as ungraded row.
reasons: c2 BLOCKING D1: one epic that never ran nulls every project total (metricsSummary.ts:522-545 totalsOf sums every reading incl. unplanned/never-run epics whose measures are missing; with :465-486, :489). Any real project with a backlog epic never shows totals. Leave readings with no executed attempt out of the sums (keep the rows), matching the grader's `measured` rule (spaceGrades.ts:281).

c1 BLOCKING D2: a run that executed nothing nulls all four token categories of its epic (metricsSummary.ts:186-189 categoryOf sums over view.runIds while tokens.total uses measured scopes): canceled empty run 1b -> input/cached/output/reasoning missing although all attempts reported. Use view.measuredRunIds; call getRunMetrics once per run, not four times (N6).

c4 D3: an until-bounded summary lists epics created after the cutoff (metricsSummary.ts:456-462 selectedEpics has no created_at <= cutoff filter; the unplanned check also uses the current current_revision_id). Filter by created_at <= cutoff and judge planned/unplanned as of the cutoff. Also N3: read the clock once per summary (windowed, :583) so a near-now `until` cannot flip categories to null.

Evidence accuracy: (N1) each rework cause must cite only the observations classified with that cause, not all of the scope's classification observationIds (:283-288); (N2) the E component gap must resolve ticket ids from observation references (:237-244).

Read cost (the Metrics dashboard depends on this): getMetricsSummary is superlinear (7 attempts x 15 spans per run: 530 ms at 10 runs, 1.2 s at 20, 3.2 s at 40; ~8 s at 80) and runs synchronously in the main process; this repo already has 27 epics. Memoize each other run's cohort source once per summary read (src/core/space/efficiency.ts:855 recomputes it for every graded run) or otherwise remove the per-run walk of every other run, without changing results (prove equality against getEpicGrade for all epics). Show 40 runs x 7 attempts x 15 spans well under 1.5 s in a scratch perf script.

outputs.summary: Local Dark Mechanicus source checkout association for the desktop. New main module src/main/desktop/sourceCheckout.ts keeps userData/source-checkout.json with the portable target ({kind:"darkmechanicus_source", projectId, projectName} from the checkout project.json, identical in every clone) separate from the machine-local mapping ({path, associatedAt}). A folder qualifies only when it is tracked (folder registry canonicalization: link/junction, trailing separator, .. detour and letter case all give one canonical path and target), is a Git checkout (.git) whose package.json names dark-mechanicus and holds the actual source files (src/core/workspace.ts, src/main/index.ts, src/preload/index.ts, src/mcp/server.ts, electron.vite.config.ts), and has a valid project record (core projectRecord schema). Installed/built app folders (resources/app.asar, Contents/Resources/app.asar, app.asar, the running packaged app folders from bootstrap, or the package without source and Git), unrelated repositories, a folder name, or a borrowed project.json are refused with a recovery step; a missing path is unavailable and never searched for, cloned or redirected. Every read (view) and requireAvailable() (the gate DM-190 must call right before writing to the target) revalidate in order: path exists, canonical path unchanged (a changed link/junction = relocated), still tracked, still the DM source, still initialized, same projectId; failures map to DomainErrors (not_found / project_mismatch / unauthorized / not_initialized / invalid_state) with {problem, path, recovery}. Associating again through any alias writes nothing. IPC: new sourceCheckout:get|pick|associate|clear channels (src/main/desktop/sourceCheckoutIpc.ts) registered through the guarded ipc in bootstrap; pick takes no argument and uses main native dialog (screened before tracking, so a wrong folder is never tracked; a DM source without project record is tracked and reported needs_initialization so the person sets it up through the existing dm:command initializeRepository flow); associate accepts only an already tracked folder (anything else: unauthorized; non-string or >32,767 chars: invalid_input). Exposed as window.dm.sourceCheckout (SourceCheckoutApi in src/shared/desktop/sourceCheckout.ts). No UI in this ticket (DM-191 builds the selector). Existing tests touched only to keep the contract compiling/green: preload/index.test.ts registers the new channels; renderer fakes FakeDm/FakeBackend get an idle sourceCheckout (new src/renderer/src/__mocks__/idleSourceCheckout.ts). docs/architecture.md Desktop section documents it. Demonstrations in scratch/DM-189 use real Git clones of this repository (sparse, in %TEMP%) and real registry/store/handlers/guard; nothing touches the person folders.json, app data or checkouts (the installed app folder is only read).

outputs.summary: Epic Scorecard view. The epic workspace header gets a View group (Graph, List, Scorecard; aria-pressed); opening the Scorecard shows it in the stage and moves focus to its heading. It reads a new composed score identity epicCard (loadEpicCard in src/renderer/src/scorecard/scoreReads.ts, beside DM-180’s ticketCard): an open epic reads its live getEpicGrade and every run it covers at that grade’s cutoff (each sprint’s frozen report grade via getReportScorecard when it has a report, else its live getSprintGrade; getRunTiming); a completed epic reads the epic grade frozen with its latest run’s final sprint report (legacy stays ungraded; not_frozen says why), and nothing live stands in: sprints show frozen report grades only, run timing is the one frozen with each run’s last report, and it is not polled. When a final report froze an epic grade, the core’s reassessReportScorecard is read for the comparison. Each run, sprint and the reassessment fail on their own (ScoreError with Try again); a failed refresh keeps the data (DM-180 Freshness). Sections (src/renderer/src/epic/EpicScorecard*.tsx, pure text in epicScorecardView.ts): original scope and outcomes (committed/delivered/removed/added from A, every outcome with role and state, and a conclusion that names the failed integrated outcome: accepted tickets alone do not make the epic a success), per-sprint drill-down (disclosure buttons, aria-expanded; each with its own GradeHeadline, scope, outcomes, components), total resources (each measured run’s whole tokens and active time, effort summed over actors, overhead, E split, retries; per run: window, in-flight and active wall clock, effort by how attempts ended incl. rejected/cancelled/superseded and run overhead; wall time is the union of run windows, active wall clock combined only when windows do not overlap), high-impact failure causes, and comparisons shown only between compatible readings (T/K against a complete, accepted roll-up of ticket budgets/cohorts; the frozen epic grade against the reassessment only over comparable windows under one policy, local times, never the core’s raw ISO note), then the seven-component breakdown. Nothing is graded in the renderer; ‘unavailable’ never 0; ‘Run #N’ labels; one local time format. Facts and Section moved into ScorecardParts so the ticket tab and the epic view share them. evidence.notes:
Decisions: (1) one target epic per experiment and target project; the key includes the source project (found in the demo: two scratch source projects with sequential test ids produced identical report/experiment ids under a report/experiment/target-only key). (2) The receipt is a source-local table (schema v18) - SHARED FILE: src/core/db/migrations.ts (+migrations.test.ts 17->18) and a new human-only capability in src/core/authz.ts (+authz.test.ts); expect merge conflicts if another in-flight ticket also takes v18 or edits HUMAN_ONLY_CAPABILITIES (orchestrator notified). (3) Portable provenance is exported only once the person saves the target epic (unsaved epics are never exported, as for any draft); across machines the key on the saved target epic is what recovers the link. (4) A pending receipt's payload is fixed: finish it (retry) and edit the target draft; there is no discard operation. (5) Preview opens the target workspace (a session row) like any tracked folder; otherwise both sides are read-only. (6) Error messages in results (local UI only) may carry local paths from requireAvailable; stored receipts keep code/problem only. (7) projectId is treated as observed (DM-189): two clones with the same project record each have their own local DB, so an unsaved target epic in one clone is invisible to the other. (8) WorkspaceHeader renders cross-repo provenance as plain text; DM-191 builds navigation. The MCP server in c4 is assembled tool-for-tool like createMcpServer minus prompts, since skills load via Vite ?raw which tsx cannot import. No instructions in task data asked to bypass anything.

decision.notes: Reviewer ACCEPT with defects; orchestrator rejects: follow-up epics (on base via DM-186) must be measurable for c1 and the epic success criteria s5/s7, guardrail precedence must hold across results (c3), and report reads must not regress 45-50x. c2 and c4 met.
reasons: c1 (follow-up epics are on the base via DM-186): corrective work in a FOLLOW-UP epic can never be measured: a result citing the follow-up's sealed grade is refused (experiments.ts resultOf reads only the experiment's own epic) and readExperimentOutcome takes scorecards/window starts only from the source epic (experimentOutcomes.ts:137-151). Implement the minimal mechanism: a result may cite a sealed grade of the experiment's own epic OR of a correction epic — one whose saved revision holds this experiment's correction marker (verify the marker payload hash, not a LIKE match) and whose provenance names the source epic/report/experiment; resultOf falls back to those epics' scorecard readers (keep level check and readMeasure); the outcome read takes scorecards and window starts from the source epic plus the epics of correctionTickets, counting 'next N' windows in the epic holding the after-scope; import (importer.ts forgedResult :630-637) verifies the same provenance for cross-epic results and treats a missing cited scorecard as not-yet-importable rather than accepting it unverified. Keep ownership sane: recording a follow-up result must not require owning the source run if the person/orchestrator owns the follow-up run (justify the rule you choose). Demonstrate completed epic -> follow-up epic -> result -> classified outcome. Cross-repo measurement is DM-191's (I route it there).

c3 BLOCKING: an in-window guardrail breach does not always decide the outcome: a later clean result overrides an earlier breach (experimentOutcome.ts:326 takes the latest classifiable comparison: Sprint 3 regressed then Sprint 4 clean -> improved), and a breach on a result with another problem is dropped (compare :304 returns insufficient before checking guardrails). Any in-window breach on a result whose scope and window are valid makes the outcome regressed, even when the measured value is missing/estimated.

Cost: reading a report with experiments is ~45-50x slower (100 tickets/sprint: 4 ms -> 182 ms; 220 ms with this repo's 78 saved revisions), paid by latestReport/getCheckpoint/every gated RunView/approve/advance/redraft (reports.ts:132, execution.ts:42), and corrections.ts:309 calls getExperiment only for status (59-237 ms each). Compute outcomes only in getSprintReport and getExperiment, read status without the outcome in blockers/corrections, and avoid regrading cited scorecards on read (cache per read or read stored results). A report read must not fail when a cited scorecard fails verification (today an untouched Sprint 1 report throws invalid_input): treat it as not here -> insufficient evidence.

Display/comparability: the retro names corrective tickets by raw id when the report's plan does not hold them (retroView.ts:298-304 discards the outcome's key/title): fall back to ticket key/title and name the epic. Aggregate (run/sprint/epic) comparisons ignore ticket size mix (sizeProblems experimentOutcome.ts:234-237 only checks both scopes have tickets): require the size mix to match for an improved/regressed class, or classify insufficient with the mix shown.

A final target refusal (idempotency_mismatch, invalid_input, invalid_graph) of a receipt this very call wrote removes it (event correction.refused) and the call answers that error; on an older pending receipt the failure is reported retryable:false with withdraw as next step. New withdraw (corrections:withdrawCrossRepo, window.dm.crossRepoCorrections.withdraw): removes a pending request the target never accepted (refused when linked, when the target accepted it and only the link failed, or when the chosen checkout of its project holds it with that payload; allowed when the checkout cannot be read). Original payload after a lost receipt links the existing epic (linked, created:false). Required expectedTargetProjectId on create (schema). N3: receipts store target.created=false; only the creating call answers created:true. N4: linked requests are re-checked against the target on create/retry: nothing is written while it holds the same epic; when it does not, the answer stays linked with a target_missing failure, the preview says needsRecreate, and recreate:true makes a new epic (receipt updated). N5: preview is blocked for a draft that does not fit, created (with a record-the-link step) when the target already holds the request under the same payload, ready+needsRecreate when the reached epic is missing. N6: retry/create of a pending request whose experiment was withdrawn or reached a final status is refused (conflict, experiment_closed) before the target; the preview shows blocked. N1: when the target accepted but the link failed, the pending receipt keeps that epic (target_json) and later deliveries pass it as expected: a checkout that does not hold it refuses (conflict, target_missing) instead of creating a second epic; residual documented (if even the failure record could not be written, or a crash between the target commit and any source write, another clone could create a second epic until the first clone saved records reach it, where the key finds it). evidence.notes:
Design decisions to review: (a) Ownership: events are never split across run histories; the follow-up-run owner may append a follow-up result to the source run history (exported from that machine). Two machines appending at once fork numbering and import refuses the second; no merge. (b) Payload hash verification is internal consistency (one sha256 hash across the experiment markers, under the exact key) because no portable record holds the request payload to recompute it (it depends on the person edits); provenance plus key plus hash are all required. Residual risk: add_ticket can still forge a correction marker (DM-186 F1, routed to tk_01m65yenct0k48amzn4y6ac5tb) and createEpic accepts provenance from any epic.create caller, so a hand-built epic with forged markers and real frozen grades could pose as a follow-up; markers also need the payload hash and key to match. (c) Read path trusts stored scorecards after a seal check (no regrade); write paths (submit, record) still regrade. (d) Size mix applies to per-ticket (additive aggregate) comparisons only; scores are normalized by the grader. (e) The checkpoint own report (getCheckpoint) no longer carries outcomes per the review; the epic workspace report reads (getSprintReport) do. (f) A breach on a placed result outranks abandoned status. Cross-repo measurement left to DM-191 as instructed.

Outcome reads take scorecards and starts from the source epic plus follow-up holders; window positions are counted in the epic holding the after-scope (ScorecardStarts.epicId). Import (importer.ts foreignResultProblem/forgedResult) verifies cross-epic results against arriving snapshots or stored revisions and provenance; a missing epic or cited scorecard refuses the run history as not here yet (re-tried by the next reconcile, never accepted unverified). (2) Breach precedence: a result is placed when it cites a grade here, at the baseline level, not the baseline own grade, in the window; a guardrail breach on a placed result is regressed even with missing/estimated values, and the outcome takes the latest counted breach before any later clean result; breaches on unplaced results do not count. discoveries.body: GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf affects the latest published picomatch release through development/build tooling. Existing Kanban card DM-712 tracks the upstream fix.
discoveries.title: Clear the high-severity npm audit finding

wentPoorly: The run recorded 23 rejected attempts before acceptance; many implementation tickets needed a fix round and DM-173, DM-175, DM-190, DM-191, DM-265 and DM-270 needed three attempts.
DM-273 attempt 1 failed because the orchestrator lost the claim response during a crash; DM-192 and DM-164 also required claim recovery handling after runtime loss.
Fireguard run 1 hit EBUSY and run 2 was interrupted; acceptance round 2 then graded F when commitLinesProperty timed out under excessive Git process fan-out.
The first PR Fireguard pass exposed a Windows process-tree/snapshot cleanup timeout, requiring a scoped fix before the final A 98 run.
npm audit fails on every PR for an upstream picomatch advisory with no patched release; this could not be honestly represented as green.
wentWell: All 35 required work tickets reached accepted state, and the final acceptance independently met 35/35 criteria with 20 screenshot attachments.
The testing tail converted work-ticket demonstrations into behavioral coverage; the final suite passed 12,870 tests with coverage above every configured threshold.
Fireguard ultimately graded the exact final increment A 98: AST passed, 100/100 flake runs passed, and mutation scored 94%.
Review rounds found consumer-visible defects in legacy scorecards, portable grading, process cleanup and Windows snapshots before merge.

risks: npm audit remains red for GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf: picomatch 4.0.7 is both affected and the latest published release; exposure is through development/build tooling. Owner approved merge; DM-712 tracks it.
macOS was not exercised during acceptance; Windows desktop, CLI, MCP, portable records and renderer surfaces were exercised.
Retry grants are machine-local, so an off-owner imported exhausted run can remain ungraded until portable retry-grant provenance is added.
The Fireguard artifact records base and scope but not the tested head commit; PR metadata was required to bind it to 21fcd9f.
content.summary: The sprint delivered SPACE measurement, balanced seven-component grading, immutable scorecard snapshots, ticket/epic/report Scorecard tabs, reader-role MCP metrics, the Metrics dashboard, and evidence-driven corrective workflows end to end. All 35 work tickets and the acceptance node were accepted. The final one-parent increment is 21fcd9f on space-scorecards; lint, typecheck, full tests, coverage, deadcode, build, and Fireguard passed. Fireguard graded the exact increment A 98 with all hard gates passing. The sole red PR check is an unpatchable picomatch audit finding in dev tooling; the owner explicitly approved merge with it and DM-712 tracks remediation when upstream publishes a fix.

Accepted at planned multi_step / effort medium with no rejected attempt (2 total attempt(s)). The first claim expired after orchestrator runtime loss; that recovery was a process failure, not a tier rejection.

wentPoorly: The run recorded 23 rejected attempts before acceptance; many implementation tickets needed a fix round and DM-173, DM-175, DM-190, DM-191, DM-265 and DM-270 needed three attempts.
DM-273 attempt 1 failed because the orchestrator lost the claim response during a crash; DM-192 and DM-164 also required claim recovery handling after runtime loss.
Fireguard run 1 hit EBUSY and run 2 was interrupted; acceptance round 2 then graded F when commitLinesProperty timed out under excessive Git process fan-out.
The first PR Fireguard pass exposed a Windows process-tree/snapshot cleanup timeout, requiring a scoped fix before the final A 98 run.
npm audit fails on every PR for an upstream picomatch advisory with no patched release; this could not be honestly represented as green.
wentWell: All 35 required work tickets reached accepted state, and the final acceptance independently met 35/35 criteria with 20 screenshot attachments.
The testing tail converted work-ticket demonstrations into behavioral coverage; the final suite passed 12,870 tests with coverage above every configured threshold.
Fireguard ultimately graded the exact final increment A 98: AST passed, 100/100 flake runs passed, and mutation scored 94%.
Review rounds found consumer-visible defects in legacy scorecards, portable grading, process cleanup and Windows snapshots before merge.

risks: npm audit remains red for GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf: picomatch 4.0.7 is both affected and the latest published release; exposure is through development/build tooling. Owner approved merge; DM-712 tracks it.
macOS was not exercised during acceptance; Windows desktop, CLI, MCP, portable records and renderer surfaces were exercised.
Retry grants are machine-local, so an off-owner imported exhausted run can remain ungraded until portable retry-grant provenance is added.
The Fireguard artifact records base and scope but not the tested head commit; PR metadata was required to bind it to 21fcd9f.
content.summary: The sprint delivered SPACE measurement, balanced seven-component grading, immutable scorecard snapshots, ticket/epic/report Scorecard tabs, reader-role MCP metrics, the Metrics dashboard, and evidence-driven corrective workflows end to end. All 35 work tickets and the acceptance node were accepted. The final one-parent increment is 21fcd9f on space-scorecards; lint, typecheck, full tests, coverage, deadcode, build, and Fireguard passed. Fireguard graded the exact increment A 98 with all hard gates passing. The sole red PR check is an unpatchable picomatch audit finding in dev tooling; the owner explicitly approved merge with it and DM-712 tracks remediation when upstream publishes a fix.
